findings.title: Async legacy write derives from cancellable request context
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create (and same pattern in Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) the goroutine does context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the incoming request context. When the API handler returns, the request context is cancelled, which immediately cancels the child context and aborts the supposedly asynchronous legacy write. The consequence is that the "safe measure" legacy backup in mode 3 is frequently skipped/cancelled, leaving legacy and unified storage divergent.

findings.title: Storage error recorded as legacy metric
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create, when d.Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) with startStorage. The failure is in storage, not legacy, so storage latency/error metrics are never emitted and legacy metrics are polluted. Operators cannot alert on or distinguish unified-storage write failures in mode 3.

findings.title: Update storage error recorded as legacy metric
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Update, the early-return path on d.Storage.Update error calls d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration. Same as Create, this misattributes unified-storage update failures to legacy, breaking dashboards/alerts for mode 3 update latency and error rate.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name as kind label
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...) passing the instance name where the kind is expected (error path correctly uses options.Kind). This creates high-cardinality metric label values (one per object name) and makes delete latency by kind unusable.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy latency recorded as storage
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go DeleteCollection the background goroutine calls d.recordStorageDuration for the legacy call instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors are counted against storage and legacy observability is lost.

findings.title: Delete discards enriched logger
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete the code builds log with name/kind/method but then does ctx=klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of using log. Request-scoped logs for delete lose name/kind/method fields, hindering debugging compared to Create/Update/Get/List.

findings.title: Legacy async create uses pre-storage input object
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create the background call is d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) using the original input obj instead of the created result returned by storage. Any defaults, resourceVersion, UID, or mutations assigned by unified storage are not propagated to legacy, guaranteeing divergence between the two stores that mode 3 is supposed to keep in sync.

findings.title: Same UpdatedObjectInfo reused concurrently for two stores
findings.body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Update the same rest.UpdatedObjectInfo objInfo is passed to d.Storage.Update synchronously and then reused in a goroutine for d.Legacy.Update. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is typically stateful/single-use and computes the new object from the old object of each store, so the second invocation can race, fail, or produce a different object than what was written to storage. The old mode 3 code snapshotted the updated object with an updateWrapper to avoid this; removing it risks corrupt/divergent legacy writes and data races.
